intro: Build your own game in Visual Studio 2019, one chapter at a time. Each chapter shows the Summit Ready code, explains every line, and then shows you how to change the code for your own game.

chapters.title: Start here
chapters.one: What Summit Ready is, what your game needs, and how this guide works.

chapters.title: Plan your game
chapters.one: Choose your client and your topic, write your requirements, and draw every window of your game.

chapters.title: Set up Visual Studio
chapters.one: Make your project in Visual Studio 2019, with the folders, files and pictures that every chapter uses.

chapters.title: Players in a text file
chapters.one: Save players to a text file, and read the players back.

chapters.title: Your own exceptions
chapters.one: Make your own exceptions, so that every wrong entry gets a clear message.

chapters.title: Register with an avatar
chapters.one: Build the Register window, where a new player picks one of 8 avatars.

chapters.title: Log in
chapters.one: Build the Log in window, which locks after 3 wrong passwords.

chapters.title: Scores, the Welcome screen and the Top 10
chapters.one: Save every score, and show the last score, the best score and the Top 10.

chapters.title: The map
chapters.one: Build the map, where a player picks each game in any order.

chapters.title: The shape of every game
chapters.one: Build a practice game with the header strip, Back to the map and the Round over box that every game uses.

chapters.title: The finish line
chapters.one: Build the Feedback window, which saves the score for the whole expedition.

chapters.title: Pack the Rucksack
chapters.one: A game chapter: a drag-and-drop game.

chapters.title: Build Knot Pairs, a memory game with cards made by code
chapters.one: You build Knot Pairs in your own project, exactly as it is in Summit Ready, and test it. Then you change it into a memory game on your own topic.
stages: See what Knot Pairs does and how a round plays
Look at the list of knots, and add the Knot class that reads it
Make the Knot Pairs form and set the form's controls
Write the game code, one method at a time
Change Knot Pairs into a game on your own topic

chapters.title: Leave No Trace
chapters.one: A game chapter: a game played with the keyboard.

chapters.title: Read the Sky
chapters.one: A game chapter: a picture quiz against the clock.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.one: A game chapter: a hidden-word game, with the cloud coming down.

chapters.title: Grid Ref Rescue
chapters.one: A game chapter: a map game with clicks and typed grid references.

chapters.title: Route Timer
chapters.one: A game chapter: a slider game that estimates how long a walk takes.

chapters.title: Listen Out
chapters.one: A game chapter: a sound is the question, and pictures are the answers.

chapters.title: Test it
chapters.one: Test every button, link and rule in your game, and keep the evidence.

chapters.title: Evaluate and hand in
chapters.one: Ask your client, judge your game against each requirement, and hand in.

filesNote: One zip holds every data file, picture and sound that Summit Ready uses. You download it once, in chapter 2. It never holds code: you write all of the code yourself.

files.name: summit-ready-files.zip
files.what: The Data, Images and Sounds folders, and credits.txt, for every chapter (8.2 MB).
